annotationRationale: Both methods organize the probability by the next jump and use reflection symmetry. Complementary exit types justify the main symmetry argument; substitution and elimination are specific to the equation alternative.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Counting & Probability is correct; no area repair is needed.

review.questionCheck: Using the standard interpretation that the four independently chosen directions are equally likely, the vertical-exit probability is 5/8, choice B. Corners cannot be the first boundary point reached. No stem, choice, key, or figure contradiction.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: Both supplied shared methods from 2020_AMC_10A_Q13 were independently verified and retained: first-jump-and-diagonal-symmetry and solve-first-step-probability-equations. The former gives a short path-reflection argument; the latter teaches a general state-equation approach. Current AoPS Solutions 1 through 3 and 4 through 5 respectively fit these routes, while LIVE supplies equivalent first-step equations.
review.annotationCheck: State-based probability and total probability are appropriate assessed concepts. Reflection is support in both routes, and complementary exits support the first route. Substitution and subtraction are correctly kept specific to the equation method.
review.areaCheck: Counting & Probability is correct; no area repair is needed.

methodReviews.mathCheck: The conditional chance of exit within three jumps is at least 1/64, so the survival bound tends to zero. Corners are inaccessible as first boundary hits. Each stated diagonal reflection preserves path probabilities and exchanges exit types, giving probability 1/2 at all three non-left first-step destinations. Thus \(1/4+(3/4)(1/2)=5/8\).
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: Correctly reuses 2020_AMC_10A_Q13/first-jump-and-diagonal-symmetry and retains its inherited aops-reference-2020_AMC_10A_Q13 credit. Current-question AoPS Solutions 1 through 3 support the route. Reuse of the credited project explanation is permitted by the supplied provenance, and source-informed-original accurately identifies its nonofficial basis.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: Termination, corner exclusion, the relevant reflection axes, and preservation of path probabilities are all explained. The four first-jump cases then follow directly, with no diagram required.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: math:recursive-counting-probability supports the first-step organization, cnm_h246 the weighted case combination, cnm_132 the path reflections, and cnm_h139 the mutually exclusive exit types with total probability one. All are used.

methodReviews.mathCheck: All four state equations match their neighboring positions and boundary outcomes. Subtraction gives \(p-q=1/4\), while \(2a+c=1/2+p+q\). Hence \(4q=3/4+2q\), so \(q=3/8\) and \(p=5/8\). The actual eventual-success probabilities satisfy these uniquely determining equations.
